# Research: Most Popular Resume Layout / CV Format in Indonesia

## Summary

Reverse-chronological ("chronological") is the dominant and most-recommended CV layout in Indonesia — every major Indonesian job platform (Jobstreet Indonesia, Indeed Indonesia, Glints, Kalibrr, KitaLulus, CakeResume) recommends it for most roles, with the combination/hybrid format a clear second for career-changers and senior roles; functional CVs are actively discouraged. Distinctively Indonesian expectations are a formal passport-style photo (3x4, neutral background), a personal-data block (place/date of birth, historically also religion and marital status — declining but still common), a 1–2 page length (1 page for fresh graduates), and conservative design (white background, dark text, one muted accent color). ATS-friendliness is now standard advice because the major Indonesian platforms process CVs digitally, but many SMEs still review manually, so the pragmatic local compromise is "simple ATS-safe layout **plus** photo."

## ⚠️ Verification caveat — read first

**No live web access was available in this run** (the `web_search`/`web_fetch` tools were absent from the runtime; confirmed by tool-not-found error). This brief is compiled from model knowledge of well-known, stable guidance published by the platforms cited. URLs below are canonical domains/category pages rather than freshly-verified article links. **Treat every citation as "well-known source, unverified this run"** and re-verify before using in the product. A ready-to-run verification checklist (exact search queries) is at the end.

---

## Findings

### 1. Layout ranking (focus: common resume layouts)

1. **Chronological (reverse-chronological) — dominant.** Indonesian platform guides and recruiter advice lead with this format: recruiters want to see career progression ("riwayat pekerjaan" in order, newest first) at a glance, and it is the easiest for both human scanning and ATS parsing. [Jobstreet Indonesia career advice](https://www.jobstreet.co.id/career-advice); [Indeed Indonesia career guide](https://id.indeed.com/career-advice/resumes-cover-letters); [Glints Blog](https://glints.com/id/blog/)
2. **Combination/hybrid — second, growing.** A skills/profile summary block on top + reverse-chronological experience. Recommended in Indonesian guides for career-changers, fresh graduates with little experience, and senior roles. [CakeResume Indonesia resources](https://www.cakeresume.com/resources); [Glints Blog](https://glints.com/id/blog/)
3. **Functional — actively discouraged.** Indonesian advice describes it as confusing for recruiters and poorly parsed by ATS; used only in niche cases. [Indeed Indonesia career guide](https://id.indeed.com/career-advice/resumes-cover-letters)

**Implication for a resume template:** default preset = reverse-chronological with an optional "ringkasan/profil" summary block (this is the local hybrid norm); offer functional only as an explicit edge-case option.

### 2. Standard section order in Indonesian CVs

The conventional local structure (in order): **Data Pribadi** (nama lengkap, contact, alamat, tempat/tanggal lahir; historically also agama + status pernikahan — now frequently omitted per modern advice), **Ringkasan/Profil** (2–3 lines), **Pendidikan**, **Pengalaman Kerja**, **Keahlian**; optional **Organisasi**, **Pelatihan/Sertifikasi**, **Referensi** ("tersedia atas permintaan"). A short profile summary at the top is a strong local norm. [Glints Blog](https://glints.com/id/blog/); [KitaLulus Blog](https://www.kitalulus.com/blog)

### 3. Platform guidance consensus (focus: platform CV-format guidance)

| Platform                       | Stance (well-known published guidance)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Jobstreet Indonesia** (SEEK) | Chronological, 1–2 pages, professional photo recommended locally, ATS-friendly simple formatting (standard headings, no tables/graphics), PDF export. [jobstreet.co.id/career-advice](https://www.jobstreet.co.id/career-advice)                                                                                             |
| **Indeed Indonesia**           | Chronological, 1–2 pages, ATS-friendly tips (standard headings, keywords from the job ad, avoid columns/header-footer text). [id.indeed.com career guide](https://id.indeed.com/career-advice/resumes-cover-letters)                                                                                                         |
| **Glints**                     | Extensive "CV ATS friendly" series; simple single-column layout, standard section names, photo optional-for-ATS but customary in Indonesia; 1–2 pages. [glints.com/id/blog](https://glints.com/id/blog/)                                                                                                                     |
| **Kalibrr**                    | CVs uploaded to Kalibrr are parsed/scanned by their platform; advice favors clean, scannable, single-column formats (their internal resume parser reads standard fields). [kalibrr.com/advice](https://www.kalibrr.com/advice)                                                                                               |
| **KitaLulus**                  | Publishes ATS-friendly CV guides and templates; simple layout, keywords, 1–2 pages. [kitalulus.com/blog](https://www.kitalulus.com/blog)                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **CakeResume Indonesia**       | Popular for tech/creative roles; modern templates, combination layout support, and ATS-friendly guidance. [cakeresume.com/resources](https://www.cakeresume.com/resources)                                                                                                                                                   |
| **LinkedIn Indonesia**         | Used heavily by Indonesian recruiters as a verification/headhunting channel; LinkedIn guidance mirrors global ATS norms (clean CV, no photo **in the document**; photo belongs on the profile). Local practice still expects the photo in the CV itself. [LinkedIn Resume Builder](https://www.linkedin.com/resume-builder/) |

**Implication:** a template that is single-column, uses standard English/Indonesian section headings, exports to PDF, and includes an optional photo block will satisfy every platform above.

### 4. Indonesian-specific design preferences (focus: colors, photos, length)

- **Photo — the single biggest local differentiator.** A formal 3x4-style photo (professional attire, neutral background) is customary and still requested in many Indonesian job ads; platform guides phrase it "recommended in Indonesia, optional for ATS." Severity: **high** if omitted in a product targeting Indonesia — most Indonesian applicants will add a photo regardless. [Jobstreet Indonesia career advice](https://www.jobstreet.co.id/career-advice)
- **Length: 1 page (fresh grads / <5 years), 2 pages acceptable for experienced.** Indonesian recruiters tolerate two pages more than Western norms, but one page is the safe default; guides consistently cap at 2 pages. [Indeed Indonesia career guide](https://id.indeed.com/career-advice/resumes-cover-letters)
- **Colors/design: conservative.** White background, black/dark-navy text, one muted accent (blue/gray); Arial/Calibri/Times New Roman; avoid tables, multi-column layouts, graphics, and header/footer text when ATS matters. Creative industries (design, marketing, content) are the exception where more visual CVs are acceptable — so offer a "creative" preset but default to conservative. [Glints Blog](https://glints.com/id/blog/); [Kalibrr Advice](https://www.kalibrr.com/advice)
- **Language:** Bahasa Indonesia for local companies; English for multinationals/tech; bilingual CVs are common. The resume-editor's EN/ID export feature matches this local norm well. [Glints Blog](https://glints.com/id/blog/)

### 5. ATS compatibility in Indonesia (focus: ATS)

- ATS adoption is real and growing: Jobstreet Indonesia runs on SEEK's platform, Kalibrr parses uploaded CVs, Glints and KitaLulus scan applications, and mid-size+ companies use commercial ATS (Workable, Greenhouse, local vendors). Standard advice therefore matches global ATS rules: **standard section headings, single column, no text-in-images, PDF or DOCX, keywords from the job description, no photo-required disclaimer.** [Jobstreet Indonesia career advice](https://www.jobstreet.co.id/career-advice); [KitaLulus Blog](https://www.kitalulus.com/blog)
- **Local nuance:** many SMEs/startups still review CVs manually, so the Western "no photo" rule is not applied in Indonesia. The local consensus is **photo + simple ATS-safe layout**, not photo-free. A template should therefore keep the photo block but place it outside any tables/columns and keep the body single-column so parsers don't break.
- **Format caveat:** for ATS, export to PDF is fine; DOCX is the most parse-safe. Text must not be embedded in images.

### 6. Recruiter-preference evidence — data is scarce (focus: surveys)

- **Explicitly: no robust public survey ranks CV layouts by Indonesian recruiter preference.** This is a data gap, not a solved question.
- Best available evidence: (a) the platform-guidance consensus above (Jobstreet/SEEK, Indeed, Glints, Kalibrr, KitaLulus all converge on chronological + 1–2 pages + simple formatting); (b) Jobstreet/SEEK employer-facing content on hiring and CV screening; (c) the widely-cited (if dated) TheLadders eye-tracking claim that recruiters spend ~6 seconds on a first CV scan — repeatedly quoted in Indonesian career articles to justify scannable, chronological one-pagers. [TheLadders 2012 eye-tracking study as cited across Indonesian career blogs](https://www.theladders.com/press)

### 7. Implications for the resume-editor template (actionable)

1. **Default preset:** reverse-chronological, single column, conservative colors (white + black/navy + one blue/gray accent), Arial/Calibri.
2. **Mandatory-by-default section:** Data Pribadi with **optional photo block** (3x4 ratio hint, neutral background) — include photo but ensure it doesn't break ATS parsing (no text in image, photo outside text columns).
3. **Sections in local order:** ringkasan/profil → pendidikan → pengalaman kerja → keahlian → (organisasi, sertifikasi, referensi optional).
4. **Length guard:** one page default with warnings beyond 2 pages; font size ≥ 10pt.
5. **Language toggle:** EN/ID section headings (matches existing app feature).
6. **Export:** PDF default, DOCX option for maximum ATS compatibility.

| Template | ATS safety | Dev-recruiter fit | No-photo fit | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reverse-chronological | Best | Good — progression visible, but tech stack sits below the fold | Good | Solid general default, wastes the top of page for a dev |
| **Combination / hybrid** (summary + skills top, experience reverse-chronological) | Good (single column, standard headings) | **Best** — stack visible in the first screen; experience still chronological | **Best** — profile + skills block substitutes for the photo's "instant identity" role | ✅ **Chosen** |
| Functional / skills-first | Weakest — poorly parsed, discouraged by every major ID platform | Mixed — niche senior/consultant use only | Medium | ❌ Rejected |

### 1.2 Reasoning

1. **Role-specific screening habits.** Dev recruiters and technical screeners in Indonesia (and globally) scan for the tech stack, years of experience, and proof of delivery — not for narrative career history. The top third of the page must contain: name → title → one-line positioning → tech stack. A pure reverse-chronological layout delays the stack until after Education, costing the recruiter's first ~6-second scan.
2. **The research already endorses hybrid as the runner-up**, specifically "for career-changers, fresh graduates with little experience, and senior roles" (research §1). Developer hiring skews exactly toward these populations (bootcamp/fresh graduates in Indonesian tech; senior ICs where depth of stack matters). Hybrid is therefore the role-scoped best fit, not a contradiction of the general default.
3. **ATS stays intact.** Single column, standard headings, comma-separated skills, real text only — a "Core Skills" section is a standard, reliably-parsed ATS section. All the research's ATS rules (§5) are preserved; only the *order* changes.
4. **Fresh-grad fit.** The optional Projects section compensates for thin experience — directly aligned with the research's note that hybrid is recommended for fresh graduates.

### 1.3 Deliberate deviation from the general ID section order — explicit

The parent research's general local order is: Data Pribadi → Ringkasan → Pendidikan → Pengalaman → Keahlian (research §2).

This template revises that order for dev roles:

- **Skills moves up** (above Experience) — stack-first scanning for technical roles.
- **Education moves down** (after Experience/Projects) — for a mid-level dev, the track record outweighs the degree; research §1 already places the hybrid format second overall, so this is a *narrowing*, not an overturn.
- **Education returns to the top** (after Summary) only for fresh graduates — implement as a preset toggle (`educationPosition: "top" | "bottom"`).

Everything else (Data Pribadi → Ringkasan first, reverse-chronological experience, conservative design, 1–2 pages) honors the research unchanged.

---

## 2. No-photo decision & mitigation

### 2.1 Does omitting the photo hurt in Indonesia?

- The photo is "the single biggest local differentiator" in *general* Indonesian CV guidance (research §4) — but that is a cross-role average. For **developer roles specifically**, the photo is the least expected: tech startups and MNCs hire via ATS pipelines and online profiles; Jobstreet/Glints guidance explicitly frames the photo as "optional for ATS"; English-language CVs for MNCs routinely omit it; LinkedIn guidance (heavily used by ID tech recruiters) says the photo belongs on the profile, not the document.
- Residual risk is real but narrow: **traditional SMEs / old-school HRD** may still expect a photo. Mitigation is a user-level toggle, not a layout compromise (see §2.3).

### 2.2 How the template compensates (design-level)

1. **Text-only header designed without a placeholder.** The header is a self-contained block: name (large, bold) + role title (accent color) + one-line positioning. No empty photo frame — a no-photo template that renders with a hole *looks* broken; this one doesn't.
2. **Links as identity.** GitHub + LinkedIn + portfolio in the header — Indonesian tech recruiters verify candidates online instead of by photo; this is the strongest substitute.
3. **Profile summary (2–3 lines)** right under the header gives the "who is this person" answer a photo would otherwise provide.
4. **Complete contact block** (phone, email, city, availability if desired).

### 2.3 App-level policy

- Preset default: `showPhoto: false`, but keep a **photo toggle** in the editor. When enabled, photo renders top-right (≈28×36mm, 3x4 ratio hint) *outside* the text flow, with no text inside the image — ATS-safe per research §5.
- Tooltip when disabled: "Photo is optional for tech roles; many Indonesian startups and MNCs do not require it. Enable if applying to companies that ask for it."
- ATS bonus of no-photo: no parser ambiguity, smaller file, faster upload, and full compliance with Western/global ATS norms.

### 3.1 Page setup

| Property | Value |

| Page size | A4 (210×297mm) — Indonesian standard |
| Margins | 14mm uniform (12–15mm acceptable) |
| Columns | 1 (no tables; skills as comma-separated lists, not bars) |
| Length | 1 page target (mid-level); auto-flow to 2 max; font ≥ 10pt |
| Font family | One family throughout: Arial (max compatibility) or Calibri; Inter acceptable for a modern look |
| Background | White (#FFFFFF) |

### 3.2 Color tokens (one accent only — conservative per research §4)

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `--bg` | `#FFFFFF` | page background |
| `--text-primary` | `#1F2430` | name, headings, body |
| `--text-secondary` | `#4A5568` | contact line, dates, metadata |
| `--accent` | `#1E5AA8` | title line, section-rule under headings, links |
| `--rule` | `#D0D7DE` | thin rules under section headings |

Contrast: `#1E5AA8` on white ≈ 6.5:1 (WCAG AA pass). No other colors.

### 3.3 Section order & headings (EN primary, ID via language toggle)

| # | Section | EN heading | ID heading | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Header | *(no heading)* | Data Pribadi | always | name, title, contact, links |
| 2 | Professional Summary | `Professional Summary` | `Ringkasan Profil` | always | 2–3 lines |
| 3 | Core Skills | `Core Skills` | `Keahlian Inti` | always | 3–4 groups, comma lists |
| 4 | Work Experience | `Work Experience` | `Pengalaman Kerja` | always | reverse-chronological |
| 5 | Projects | `Projects` | `Proyek` | on (dev roles) | 2–3 items; off if space is tight |

| 7 | Certifications | `Certifications` | `Sertifikasi` | optional | only relevant certs |

ATS note: English headings parse most reliably across the platforms in research §3; if the job ad is in Indonesian, ID headings are acceptable, but EN is safer. The app's existing EN/ID export feature maps 1:1 onto this.

### 3.4 Typography spec

| Element | Font / size / weight | Style |
|---|---|---|
| Name | 19pt bold, `--text-primary` | single line, no middle name clutter |
| Title line | 11.5pt, `--accent` | e.g. `Backend Software Engineer · Node.js · TypeScript` |
| Contact / links | 9.5–10pt, `--text-secondary` | one line: phone · email · city; second line: GitHub · LinkedIn · portfolio |
| Section heading | 12pt bold, `--text-primary` | 0.6pt bottom rule in `--accent`; margin-top 10pt, margin-bottom 4pt |
| Body | 10–10.5pt, line-height 1.35 | bullets 3–5 per role, max one nesting level |
| Dates | 9.5pt, `--text-secondary`, right-aligned on the same line as role/company | format `Mar 2022 – Present` / `Mar 2022 – Sekarang` |

### 3.5 Section content specs

**Header (no heading):**
- Line 1: full name.
- Line 2: role title + top-3 stack keywords.
- Line 3: `+62 812-XXXX-XXXX · email@domain.com · Jakarta, Indonesia`.
- Line 4: `github.com/username · linkedin.com/in/username · portfolio-url` (only real links; omit if absent).

**Professional Summary (2–3 lines):** line 1 = years + role + industry; line 2 = stack breadth + one strength; line 3 = one measurable outcome. Example EN: "Backend engineer with 4+ years building APIs and microservices for fintech products. Strong in Node.js/TypeScript with PostgreSQL and AWS. Reduced API p95 latency by 40% at PT Teknologi Maju."

**Core Skills:** max 4 groups, comma-separated (ATS-parses as keywords; no skill bars):
- `Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, SQL`
- `Frameworks: Node.js, NestJS, Express, React (basic)`
- `Data & Infra: PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker, AWS (EC2, S3, Lambda)`
- `Tools: Git, GitHub Actions, Jest, Kubernetes (basic)`

**Work Experience:** per role — role title, company, city, dates (MM/YYYY). 3–5 bullets, strong verb + action + metric; mention the stack used per role (ATS keywords live here too). Example bullet ID: "Mengurangi response time API sebesar 40% dengan optimasi query PostgreSQL dan caching Redis." Dates: newest first; `Present`/`Sekarang` for current role.

**Projects (dev-specific, default on):** name (hyperlinked), one-line description, stack tags, one impact bullet max. 2–3 items. This section is the fresh-grad equalizer.

**Education:** degree, major, university, city, year. GPA + relevant coursework only for fresh grads (<1 year experience).

**Certifications / Languages (optional):** cert = name, issuer, year; languages = `Bahasa Indonesia (native) · English (professional)`. Only include certs relevant to the target stack.
